entries.appliesTo: generation services and covered platforms distributing counterfeit intimate images

dutySources.consent-workflow: § 13-72b-201(3) — 'a generation service shall implement and maintain a consent system that: (a) requires the identifiable individual depicted in the counterfeit intimate image to affirmatively provide consent before the counterfeit intimate image is distributed'
dutySources.takedown-process: § 13-72b-302(1) — 'A covered platform shall establish and implement notice and removal procedures that comply with the requirements established in Section 3(a) of the Take It Down Act'; § 13-72b-205(2) — 'A generation service shall clearly and conspicuously provide to users procedures for reporting violations to the generation service.'
dutySources.risk-program: § 13-72b-205(3)(a) — 'A generation service shall publish in a clear and conspicuous location on the generation service's website or primary user interface: (a) the written policy required by Subsection 13-72b-203(1)(b)'
dutySources.content-safeguards: § 13-72b-203(1)(b)(ii) — 'includes reasonable safeguards designed to prevent the creation of counterfeit intimate images'; § 13-72b-205(3)(b) — 'a general description of the safeguards implemented to prevent the generation of non-consensual counterfeit intimate images'

exposure.enforcer: private-right-of-action (actual + punitive damages, attorney fees, injunction)

sources.consentRequired: § 13-72b-201(2) — 'A generation service may not distribute a counterfeit intimate image without first obtaining consent from the identifiable individual depicted in the counterfeit intimate image.'
sources.coveredSubjects: § 13-72b-101(8) — '"Identifiable individual" means an individual who is recognizable as an actual human individual by the human individual's face, likeness, or other distinguishing characteristic'
sources.enforcer: § 13-72b-202(1) — 'A person, or the heirs of a deceased person, who has been injured by a violation recognized in Section 13-72b-201 may bring a civil action against the generation service that committed the violation.'; § 13-72b-303(1) (same for covered platforms)

flags: family-fit: this is an NCII (counterfeit-intimate-image) regime, but coded likeness-rights because it is civil and imposes ongoing company compliance duties; ai-crimes is reserved for criminal prohibitions per rule 10 and this chapter creates no criminal offense

content-safeguards and risk-program (written policy) are formally safe-harbor conditions under § 13-72b-203(1)(b), but § 13-72b-205(3) calls the policy 'required' and mandates publishing it and the safeguards description
consent records must be kept 'for a period of not less than seven years' (§ 13-72b-201(3)(c)) — no retention param key in vocabulary
§ 13-72b-205(1) duty to 'inform users that: (a) distribution of non-consensual counterfeit intimate images is prohibited' fits no listed duty key (not disclosure-ui, which is AI-in-use labeling)
48-hour takedown deadline: § 13-72b-302(2)(c) 'removing the reported counterfeit intimate image within 48 hours after receiving the notice' — no param key

no penaltyMax: remedies are uncapped actual damages ('including damages for emotional distress'), punitive damages if 'willful, reckless, or malicious', and attorney fees; 'Each distribution... constitutes a separate violation' (§ 13-72b-202(5))
extensive defendant protections: safe harbors (§§ 13-72b-203, 13-72b-304), heightened pleading standards with mandatory dismissal and fee-shifting (§§ 13-72b-204, 13-72b-305)
Chapter 72b is NOT added to the Division of Consumer Protection's enforcement list in § 13-2-1(2) (only Chapter 72c is) — enforcement is private civil action only

entries.appliesTo: large online platforms, capture device manufacturers, and covered generative-AI providers

dutySources.detection-tool: § 13-72c-201(1)(a) — 'detect whether compliant system provenance data is embedded into or attached to content distributed on the large online platform'; (1)(c) — 'allow a user to inspect all available compliant system provenance data in an easily accessible manner'
dutySources.disclosure-ui: § 13-72c-201(1)(b) — 'provide a user interface to disclose the availability of system provenance data'
dutySources.watermarking: § 13-72c-203 — 'A covered provider shall include a latent disclosure in image, video, or audio content, or content that is any combination of image, video, or audio, created or substantially modified by the covered provider's generative artificial intelligence system'; § 13-72c-202(1) — 'A capture device manufacturer shall include a latent disclosure in content captured by the capture device'

sources.watermark: § 13-72c-203 — 'A covered provider shall include a latent disclosure in image, video, or audio content'
sources.detectionTool: § 13-72c-201(1)(a) — 'A large online platform shall: (a) detect whether compliant system provenance data is embedded into or attached to content distributed on the large online platform'
sources.disclosureTrigger: § 13-72c-203 — 'in image, video, or audio content, or content that is any combination of image, video, or audio, created or substantially modified by the covered provider's generative artificial intelligence system'
sources.penaltyMax: § 13-72c-301(2)(a) — 'the division director may impose an administrative fine of up to $2,500 for each violation of this chapter'
sources.enforcer: § 13-72c-301(1) — 'The Division of Consumer Protection shall administer and enforce the provisions of Part 2, Content Provenance Standards and Requirements'

flags: two user thresholds, lossy single param: covered provider (genAI, watermarking duty) at 'over 1,000,000 monthly visitors or users' vs large online platform (detection/disclosure duties) at 'exceeded 2,000,000 unique monthly users during the preceding 12 months' (§ 13-72c-101(8)(a)); userThreshold coded to the covered-provider figure
anti-stripping prohibition fits no duty key: § 13-72c-201(2) 'may not, to the extent technically feasible, knowingly strip any system provenance data or digital signature'

capture-device duty starts later: § 13-72c-202(4) 'applies to any capture device a capture device manufacturer produces for sale in the state on or after January 1, 2028'; manufacturer 'may provide a user with the option to disable the latent disclosure' (§ 13-72c-202(2))

duties qualified by feasibility/standards: 'only to the extent technically feasible and compliant with widely adopted specifications adopted by an established standards-setting body' (§ 13-72c-202(3)); covered-provider disclosure 'to the extent that it is technically feasible and reasonable' (§ 13-72c-203(1))

additional penalty: 'A court may impose a civil penalty of no more than $5,000 for each violation of an administrative or court order' (§ 13-72c-301(5)) — order-violation penalty, not coded as penaltyMax
covered-provider carve-out: excludes systems 'used exclusively for the person's internal business operations and is not made publicly accessible' (§ 13-72c-101(5)(b))

entries.appliesTo: state agencies (via chief information officer rulemaking on webpage digital content)

dutySources.watermarking: § 63A-16-215(2) — 'The standards required by Subsection (1) shall require a digitally accessible provenance record containing provenance information for digital content captured, created, or edited'

sources.program: § 63A-16-215(1) — 'The chief information officer shall make rules... establishing standards for digital content on a webpage of a state agency that the public can access to facilitate a transaction or obtain a service'

flags: rulemaking is conditional: standards required only 'if the chief information officer determines there is a substantial risk that fraudulent or misleading media could cause harm to a resident of the state interacting with the state agency' (§ 63A-16-215(1))
'This section does not apply to digital content created before January 1, 2027.' (§ 63A-16-215(3))
no exposure block: section states no penalty or enforcement mechanism
